name: Yelagiri Hills
description: A small, affordable hill station with 14 hairpin bends, Punganoor lake boating, orchards and trekking trails on Swamimalai. Quiet and easy for a weekend break from Chennai or Bengaluru.

name: Vellore Fort and Jalakandeswarar Temple
description: A 16th-century fort surrounded by a wide moat, with a Vijayanagara-style temple inside whose carved pillars and mandapam are the highlight. A good history stop with open lawns and a small museum.

name: Sripuram Golden Temple
description: A modern temple covered in gold, set in a landscaped star-shaped path surrounded by gardens. Calm and spiritual, best visited in the evening when the gold glows under lights.

name: Pulicat Lake Bird Sanctuary
description: One of the largest brackish lagoons in India, with flamingos, pelicans and other migratory birds in the cooler months. Quiet boat trips and an old Dutch cemetery make it a peaceful half-day trip from Chennai.

name: Elliot's Beach, Besant Nagar
description: A clean, relaxed city beach with cafes, street food and the Ashtalakshmi temple nearby. Calmer than Marina, popular for evening walks and sunrise.

name: Fort St. George
description: The first English fortress in India, built in 1644 and now home to the state secretariat and a museum of colonial-era artefacts. A compact history stop in central Chennai.

name: Kolli Hills
description: A remote hill range reached by 70 hairpin bends, with the Agaya Gangai waterfall, herbal gardens and cool, uncrowded forests. Good for travellers who want nature without tourist crowds.

name: Topslip and Anamalai Tiger Reserve
description: A forest area of teak and bamboo in the Anamalai hills with elephant camps, jeep safaris and chances to see gaur, deer and lion-tailed macaques. Forest department stays make it good for a nature-focused trip.

name: Adiyogi Statue and Isha Yoga Center
description: A huge Shiva bust at the foot of the Velliangiri hills, with the Dhyanalinga meditation hall and quiet grounds. Popular for meditation, yoga programmes and the evening light show.

name: Marudhamalai Murugan Temple
description: A hilltop Murugan temple on the edge of Coimbatore with forested surroundings, steps and a road up. A short, peaceful stop with views over the city and hills.

name: Kotagiri
description: The quietest of the three main Nilgiri hill towns, with tea estates, Catherine Falls and Kodanad viewpoint. Cool weather and slow, uncrowded sightseeing make it good for relaxed trips.

name: Monkey Falls and Aliyar Dam
description: A forest-fringed waterfall near Pollachi with bathing allowed when the flow is safe, plus Aliyar Dam with gardens and a fish-fry stall culture below. A relaxed day trip combining nature and local food.

name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
description: A 17th-century palace of the Madurai Nayak king, known for its huge pillars and a vast courtyard with arches. A light-and-sound show is held in the evening.

name: Alagar Kovil
description: A Vishnu temple set at the foot of a forested hill about 20 km from Madurai, linked to the Chithirai festival. Quiet and green, with a nearby hill shrine, good for pairing with a city day.

name: Palani Murugan Temple
description: One of the most visited Murugan temples, on a hilltop reached by steps, a winch train or a ropeway. Known for the Panchamirtham prasadam and sweeping views of the plains.

name: Pillar Rocks and Guna Caves
description: Three granite cliffs rising about 120 metres near Kodaikanal, and the deep boulder caves nearby. Misty viewpoints and pine forests make this a good extension to a Kodaikanal day.

name: Meghamalai
description: The Cloud Mountain, a remote plateau of tea and cardamom estates, lakes and misty forests with very few tourists. Great for people who want silence and cool weather.

name: Suruli Falls
description: A tall waterfall in the Western Ghats near Cumbum that drops into a pool and feeds a cave temple. Best when the river flows well, with forest stalls and short walks nearby.

name: Thiruchendur Murugan Temple
description: A Murugan temple right on the Bay of Bengal shore, with a tall gopuram and sea-bathing before the darshan. Combines pilgrimage and beach atmosphere.

name: Manapad
description: A quiet fishing village with a white church on a rocky point, long empty beaches and calm sea views. Good for sunsets, photography and relaxed seaside time.

name: Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
description: A large Western Ghats reserve of dense forest, rivers and waterfalls with tigers, elephants and lion-tailed macaques. Trekking and jeep trips need permits from the forest department.

name: Thiruparappu Falls
description: A broad, popular waterfall with a swimming pool beside it and a nearby Shiva temple. Easy to reach from Kanyakumari, ideal for a refreshing break from the heat.

name: Padmanabhapuram Palace
description: A wooden palace of the Travancore kings, known for its carved ceilings, mural paintings and polished floors. One of the finest examples of traditional Kerala-style architecture in Tamil Nadu.

name: Muttom Beach
description: A scenic beach with black rocks, a lighthouse and a dramatic meeting of waves and cliffs. Quieter than Kanyakumari and good for photography and sunset.

name: Pamban Bridge
description: India's first sea bridge, connecting the mainland to Rameswaram island, with a railway lift span and a road bridge beside it. A great stop for sea views and photos on the way to Rameswaram.

name: Thanjavur Maratha Palace and Saraswathi Mahal Library
description: A palace complex with the Durbar Hall, an art gallery of Chola bronzes and a library of rare manuscripts. A good indoor history stop in Thanjavur next to the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

name: Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram
description: A 12th-century Chola temple in the UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples group, famous for its fine stone carvings and a chariot-shaped mandapa. Smaller and quieter than Thanjavur's big temple.

name: Nataraja Temple, Chidambaram
description: An ancient Shiva temple dedicated to Nataraja, the dancing form, with four large gopurams and a golden-roofed sanctum. An important spiritual and cultural centre, easy to combine with Pichavaram.

name: Rock Fort Temple, Tiruchirappalli
description: A temple complex built on a massive rock rising over the city, reached by about 400 steps cut into the stone. The top gives panoramic views of Trichy and the Cauvery.

name: Tharangambadi (Tranquebar)
description: A quiet seaside town with a 17th-century Danish fort, old colonial buildings and a calm beach. Relaxed, uncrowded and good for history and sea breeze.

name: Gingee Fort
description: A fortress spread across three hills, known as the Troy of the East, with granary, temples and a steep climb to the top. Great for trekking, sunrise and history lovers.
